haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store, and its output is never charged.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes its invoices into the shadow store and never calls the payment provider.
haiku-low.q3: Gate A: each of the last 7 consecutive days has a mismatch rate under 0.1%, totaling at least 5,000 invoices. On-call promotes, and the rollout tool checks the rows.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's payment failure rate exceeds 2% over 10 minutes. This applies only in both or new_only, never shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over again, on-call must promote to shadow, and gate A must be met from scratch.
haiku-low.q6: Once 35 days have passed since new_only began, the rollout tool rejects every rollback. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so catch-up needs the full log.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode at the start of each invoice, so an in-progress invoice finishes in its starting mode. They read charging_paused before each payment call.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence is kept in comparison_results, written nightly. The rollout tool checks these rows before writing billing_mode and refuses promotions that skip a mode or fail the gate.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor detects it. It measures the new engine's payment-call failure rate over a 10-minute sliding window. Above 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Due invoices are recorded as pending, not charged. The old engine charges them at resume_charging, after reconcile, once charging_paused is set to false.
haiku-low.q11: Reconcile prevents re-charging. Invoices the new engine already charged with matching totals are marked settled. Mismatched totals go to the Finance review queue, not an automatic re-charge.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in rolling_back with charging paused. On-call is paged, and the failed step is retried from the rollback record, since steps are safe to repeat.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: each of the last 7 consecutive days has a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and together those days compared at least 5,000 invoices (only rows after the latest entry into shadow count). On-call promotes, through the rollout tool.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts it through the rollout tool and pages on-call. It does so when the new engine's payment-provider call failure rate goes above 2% over a sliding 10-minute window, in `both` or `new_only` modes (not shadow).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in `old_only`. To take over again, on-call must promote to `shadow` and gate A must be met from scratch (gate counts reset), then continue through the promotions.
sonnet.q6: It stops being possible 35 days after `new_only` began, because usage events are kept only 35 days and catch-up needs every event since new_only began. After that the rollout tool rejects every rollback, manual or automatic.
sonnet.q7: Workers read `billing_mode` at the start of each invoice. An invoice already in progress finishes under the mode it started in.
sonnet.q8: In the `comparison_results` table, which the nightly comparison job writes one row per night to. Gate B also needs a Finance sign-off recorded in the rollout tool. The rollout tool checks these rows before writing `billing_mode` and refuses any promotion that skips a mode or fails its gate.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the failure rate of the new engine's payment-provider calls over a sliding 10-minute window. If it goes above 2% in `both` or `new_only`, it starts a rollback through the rollout tool and pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: After charging is paused, invoices that fall due are written to the ledger as pending instead of being charged (a payment call already in flight finishes). They are charged by the old engine after `resume_charging` sets `charging_paused` to false, once the rollout is in `old_only`.
sonnet.q11: The reconcile step. Each new-engine ledger invoice is matched with the old engine's invoice for the same customer and billing period. If it was already charged and the totals agree, it is marked settled and never charged again. If the totals differ, it goes to the Finance review queue and is not re-charged automatically.
sonnet.q12: The rollout stays in `rolling_back` with charging paused, and the new engine never gets charging back. On-call is paged, and the failed step is retried from the rollback record. Each step records its progress and is safe to repeat. Charges are delayed, never dropped or doubled.
